description: This is our first NASA Space Apps Challenge, and we’re excited to learn, experiment, and build something meaningful together. As students from different backgrounds, we’re bringing our skills, creativity, and ideas together to tackle a real-world challenge using NASA’s open data.
summary:
TriFlow is an onboard health-monitoring tool for long-duration missions. In 2016, Scott Kelly came back from 340 days on the ISS struggling to walk, despite about two hours of exercise a day: exercise alone is not enough, astronauts need to know which effort, when, and for which organ.

TriFlow works on three axes. (1) Body analysis: a daily whole-body ultrasound scan concept, combined with blood, urine and Apple Watch data, displayed on an interactive 3D anatomical body. (2) An optimized daily routine: every reading is checked against NASA-STD-3001 thresholds, three machine-learning models project bone, muscle and heart loss up to Mars arrival and mission end, and the app turns this into today's plan, with a "Why?" that cites the NASA standard. (3) Psychological follow-up: continuous capture analysed by AI observers and AI psychologists, with the decision always left to a human psychologist.

Everything runs onboard, offline. The demo follows a fictional commander on day 94 of an 860-day Mars mission: his data are simulated, while the standards, published loss rates, a blood-age model trained on 9,326 real NHANES adults and the live Apple Watch heart rate are real.
details: WHAT IT DOES TriFlow tells an astronaut, every morning and without waiting for Earth, how their body is doing, what to do today, and why. It has three axes: 1. Body analysis: a daily whole-body ultrasound scan (concept based on the ultrasound scanner announced by Midjourney Medical in June 2026), blood and urine tests, and an Apple Watch. The "Body" page shows an interactive 3D anatomical body (Z-Anatomy models) with skeleton, muscles, organs, cardiovascular and nervous layers. Each organ opens a window with today's metrics, its NASA threshold, its weekly slope, an estimated biological age gap and a projection up to mission end. 2. Optimized daily routine: the "War Room" page turns the morning check-in and the latest data into today's plan (exercise on the ARED, cycle or treadmill, meals, tests). Every recommendation has a "Why?" link that goes down to the NASA-STD-3001 requirement it comes from. The Apple Watch app shows the plan of the day, the body at a glance and a to-do list, and streams the real heart rate to the War Room. 3. Psychological follow-up: the "Mental Health" page shows a prototype where connected glasses capture the day continuously; 3 AI observers extract facts without interpreting, 3 AI psychologists each give a level (kept when 2 of 3 agree), and a human psychologist receives the file and decides. The astronaut cannot switch the signal off, so a disorder cannot be hidden to keep a seat on the mission. HOW IT WORKS - Alerts are rules, not AI: every status (green, amber, red) comes from a NASA-STD-3001 threshold. - Three machine-learning models (Python, scikit-learn), applied offline in the browser: (A) blood age, ElasticNet regression trained on 9,326 real adults from NHANES (CDC); (B) organ projection, quantile regression giving a favourable / likely / unfavourable case for bone, muscle and heart at Mars arrival (day 210) and mission end (day 860), trained on 2,000 virtual astronauts calibrated on published NASA loss rates, and beating a fixed-curve baseline on all 12 projections; (C) mood signal, logistic regression comparing the astronaut to their own baseline. - Real communication delay from NASA JPL Horizons (about 11 minutes one way on day 94). DEMO SCENARIO Commander Haddad is fictional: day 94 of an 860-day Mars mission. His data are simulated and clearly labelled "Simulated" in the app. The standards, the published loss rates, the NHANES training data and the live Apple Watch heart rate are real. In the mental-health prototype, a disorder injected on day 75 is flagged on day 85, with zero false alerts for a healthy control astronaut. BENEFITS AND IMPACT Following the plan every day halves the projected hip bone loss at mission end (4.2 % instead of 8.7 %). The tool works offline, explains every recommendation, keeps a human in the loop for every medical or psychological decision, and can be retrained as soon as real astronaut data become available. TOOLS TypeScript, React, Vite, three.js (react-three-fiber), Z-Anatomy 3D models (CC BY-SA 4.0), Python and scikit-learn, Swift/SwiftUI for watchOS, Vitest, Vercel. AI coding assistants were used to write code; the mental-health prototype uses the Claude API to run the AI observers and psychologists on simulated days. CREATIVITY A 3D "digital twin" anchored on NASA standards rather than black-box scores, a "Why?" for every action, a multi-agent psychological pipeline with a mandatory human decision, and an honest Real / Simulated label on every number.
